intelligence.title: It's Not What You Do — It's How You Do It

intelligence.essence: A smart app is not one page, and it is not every feature dumped onto one surface. It is ONE app composed of smart blocks — pages within pages, blocks within blocks — where the home stays light, every function sits behind a clear button, and the layout itself is the intelligence. A feature's presence is worth nothing without its placement: it is not what you do, it is how you do it.
intelligence.human_view: Tonight the three flagship models shipped with every standard feature working — messaging, inbox, invites, reports, install, all of it — and Shawn rejected them on sight: "you failed… not logical, not sensible, not intelligent, not organized." He was right. The build had stacked a second complete app on top of the page: its own banner-hero with a big profile picture, its own menus, its own tabs, with the actual page living underneath. Every box on the feature checklist was ticked, and the experience was a mess. Then he taught the standard plainly: one app does not mean one page — it means one app, made of blocks, easy to operate, everything intentional.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine building a house by putting a second whole house on top of the first one because the second house has a kitchen you like. It has all the rooms — and nobody can live in it. A good house has one front door, one hallway, and rooms you walk into one at a time. An app is the same: one entrance, clear doors, one room at a time.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, having every pot and pan you own sitting out on the counter doesn't make it a good kitchen — it makes it a cluttered one. A good kitchen has everything put in its place, easy to reach when you need it, and the counter clear. That's all this is: everything in its place, nothing piled up, and the important things where they belong.
intelligence.naya_view: Verify a page the way a human meets it, not the way a checklist reads it. The flagship verification measured features present and geometry correct — and never asked the only question that mattered: is this ONE app, composed with intention? Composition is a verification axis of its own: one chrome, one navigation, cover first, home light, every function behind an obvious button, install inside Settings, nothing above the fold that doesn't belong there. A block is a clonable unit — the same block, behaving the same way, in every app the factory makes.
intelligence.ai_view: The factory's promise is not features — plenty of tools have features. The promise is extraordinary experiences, assembled from blocks so good that putting them together is itself the craft. Composition is where intelligence becomes visible: what leads, what waits behind a button, what stays quiet at the bottom. Two systems glued together, or one page carrying everything at once, both fail the same test — nobody thought about how a person would actually move through it.

machine_view.title: It's Not What You Do — It's How You Do It
machine_view.machine_section:
composition_standard:
  unit: smart_block = an OBJECT with its own identity (named, official building block; repeatable, clonable, template-grade)
  interconnection: blocks are designed to connect; placement is part of a block's design — it is obvious where each block goes because it was composed to go there (elite pieces, placed in the elite place, in the elite way)
  structure: one app shell (one chrome, one navigation) containing blocks as in-app pages/views
  home: cover + primary content + entry buttons only; no function block rendered fully open by default
  access: every function reachable in one tap from a visible, labeled button/tab
  placement_laws: install and identity editing live inside the Settings block only; nothing promotional above the fold
  acceptance: feature_present AND feature_placed AND one_system AND home_light — all four required; presence alone never passes
